clue.text: Vigorous pair of judges — second one snubbing queen

parts.note: to hear and to try are both things a judge does to a case; the first of the pair is hear

indicators.note: snubbing means ignoring, so the letter for queen is left out

parts.note: the second of the pair of judging verbs is try
R is the abbreviation for queen (Regina)

explanation.surface: Two judges sit on a bench, and the junior one cold-shoulders the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbing' removes R from TRY, leaving TY. The pair of judges are verbs, not people: a judge hears and tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty and vigorous are synonyms, both describing energetic, robust action.

clue.text: Demanding Conservative remains ready

parts.note: a demanding task is a hard one
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A tough Tory is left fully prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready is slang for money available at once, the same as cash in hand.

clue.text: Shock request to ban drug

indicators.note: to ban something is to keep it out, so the drug's letter is removed

parts.note: an appeal is a request
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified by a petition to outlaw a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock or horrify someone; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Lifting curse not hard the Chinese way

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the letters so they read upward, bottom to top
not here tells us the letter for hard is absent

parts.note: an oath can be a swear word, a curse
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Removing a hex reveals the path of Chinese philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: OATH without H is OAT; 'Lifting' turns it upward in this down clue to give TAO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tao, literally 'the way', is the central principle of Chinese Taoist philosophy.

clue.text: About time to make arrangement of ragtime artist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the time letter
an arrangement of music rearranges, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A musician finds it's high time to arrange some ragtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement of' shuffles RAGTIME into MAGRITE, and 'About' puts that round T to give MAGRIT-T-E.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was a Belgian surrealist painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Making United a league leader by dishonesty

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so this takes the opening letter of league

parts.note: lying is dishonesty

explanation.surface: A football club is accused of cheating its way to the top of the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Manchester United and a football league; 'Making United' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Allying means joining together in alliance, that is, making united.

clue.text: Object found in resort meant to be drunk

indicators.note: being drunk suggests reeling and disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A holiday spot where something was supposed to be consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to protest, which is what remonstrating means; both are verbs.

clue.text: Manage to take revolutionary into not revolutionary club

indicators.note: into means the run of letters is placed inside the other piece
revolutionary here means turning round, so the word not is read backwards

parts.note: the word not as written
to run a business is to manage it
Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel leader is brought into an anti-revolutionary club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' does two different jobs: first CHE, then the signal turning NOT into TON. RUN + CHE go 'into' TON.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short heavy stick carried by police, a kind of club.

clue.text: One-time journalist and artist finding room for discussion

parts.note: ex means former, one-time
ED is short for editor, the crossword's journalist
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A former reporter and a painter find somewhere to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An exedra is a recess or room with seating used for conversation in classical buildings.

clue.text: Girl greeting reputedly happy boy heartlessly

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the heart, the central letter of the name

parts.note: the saying 'happy as Larry' makes Larry the proverbially happy boy

explanation.surface: A girl says hello to a cheerful lad in an unkind way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy as Larry' is an idiom for very happy. 'heartlessly' drops LARRY's middle R, leaving LARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary is a given name used for girls, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Predatory men found in partial disarray

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the other letters
disarray means disorder, so the letters of partial are shuffled

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the crossword's men (soldiers)

explanation.surface: Aggressive men are discovered in a state of partial chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' is OR, the other ranks of the army. 'disarray' makes the anagram RAPTIAL, and OR goes inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Raptorial describes birds of prey and other animals adapted for seizing prey, so predatory.

clue.text: Black eye following second service

indicators.note: following tells us the service word comes after the short time

parts.note: mo, a moment, is a second
use is service, as in 'of use'

explanation.surface: A boxer gets a shiner just after his second serve.
explanation.walkthrough: MOUSE is slang for a black eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouse is informal slang for a bruised, swollen eye, the injury called a shiner.

clue.text: Party role loosely associated with cabinet

indicators.note: loosely means not tightly arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political role loosely tied to the cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' shuffles ROLE together with CABINET.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebration is a festive gathering, which is one sense of a party.

clue.text: What sportsman may assume must get better after wretched delivery

indicators.note: after places the better word behind the others

parts.note: base means low and wretched
a ball is a delivery in cricket
to cap is to better, to outdo

explanation.surface: An athlete must improve after bowling badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assume' means put on, as with clothing; a cricket delivery is a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A baseball cap is headgear a sportsman may put on, assume meaning don.

clue.text: What could motorists be reversing?

indicators.note: reversing means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A puzzle about drivers backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation; turned round it gives a vehicle motorists could be in while reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is the vehicle motorists drive and could be backing up.

clue.text: To meet, for example, about it is fine

indicators.note: about means going round the other letters

parts.note: say means for example
'tis is the old contraction of it is
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An appointment is arranged and everything about it is okay.
explanation.walkthrough: SAY goes 'about' TIS and F.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy a demand or need is to meet it; the two verbs share this sense.

clue.text: Pretty royal daughter raised as an exasperating twelve-year-old

parts.note: twee means quaintly pretty

indicators.note: raised in a down clue lifts the letters so they read upward

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters, so a royal daughter

explanation.surface: A dainty princess grows up to become an irritating preteen.
explanation.walkthrough: REGAN, King Lear's daughter, is 'raised' to give NAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweenager is a child between about ten and twelve, often seen as annoying.

clue.text: He may be left when horse is extremely upset

definitions.text: He may be left when horse is
definitions.meaning: when the word horse has its insides removed, only its first and last letters H and E remain

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a reverse clue: 'horse' with its middle taken out (that is, gutted) leaves HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutted is British slang for devastated or bitterly disappointed.

clue.text: Ready to drop bowler to secure European sporting tie

parts.note: someone exhausted and ready to drop is dead on their feet

indicators.note: to secure is to hold in, so the hat surrounds the European letter

parts.note: a bowler is a hat

explanation.surface: An exhausted cricketer holds on for a draw against a European side.
explanation.walkthrough: The bowler is a hat, not a cricketer; HAT goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race in which competitors finish level, a sporting tie.

clue.text: Abuse coming from cruciverbalists

indicators.note: coming from signals the answer is taken out of the inside of the next word

explanation.surface: Insults hurled by crossword fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbal is British slang for spoken insults, as in 'giving someone verbal'.

clue.text: Delightful island short book's written about

indicators.note: written about means written round the other way, backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
vol is the short form of volume, a book

explanation.surface: An island guide is described as charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' turns the whole run ELBA + VOL backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovable means easy to love, so charming or delightful.

clue.text: Toast popular during bash

indicators.note: during means the popular word comes inside

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly, to bash
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A trendy toast raised at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: SLÁINTE is the Gaelic drinking toast, meaning 'health'. 'bash' looks like a party, but it means criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: Slainte is a Gaelic toast meaning good health, said before drinking.

clue.text: It produces catkins of a pale yellow or brown colour

definitions.text: of a pale yellow or brown colour

explanation.definitionFit: A sallow is a kind of willow; sallow skin is an unhealthy yellowish shade.

clue.text: One training as chef pledges to drop temperature

indicators.note: to drop means to leave out the letter for temperature

parts.note: commits means pledges

explanation.surface: A trainee cook promises to turn the heat down.
explanation.definitionFit: A commis is a junior chef in a professional kitchen, still learning the trade.

clue.text: Keep what's regularly not won

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep whatever they did not win.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to keep it as your possession.

clue.text: Composed, as was boss on stage

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the boss word after the stage word

parts.note: a level is a stage, as in a game
to head something is to boss it, so headed means acted as boss

explanation.surface: A calm performer bosses the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' sounds theatrical but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: A level-headed person is calm and sensible, that is, composed.

clue.text: Aim to secure fine, rising woman

indicators.note: rising in a down clue reads the letters upward
to secure means holding something within, so fine goes inside

parts.note: an end is an aim
A1 means first-rate, fine; written AI

explanation.surface: Determined to get a top fine, a woman climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (written AI) is 'first-rate'. END secures AI to make ENAID, which 'rising' turns upward into DIANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Diane is a female given name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: Spells in Havana ending differently after retirement

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so the letters are read backwards
ending differently means the last letter is changed to another

parts.note: a Havana is a Cuban cigar

explanation.surface: A Cuban smoke tastes different after you retire.
explanation.walkthrough: Change CIGAR's last letter to give CIGAM; 'after retirement' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic is the casting of spells, so spells serve as a definition by example.

clue.text: Elaborate on zebra say making come-back in prehistoric period

indicators.note: elaborate means worked out in detail, so these letters are reworked
making a come-back means turning back, so the letters reverse

parts.note: eg (for example) means say

explanation.surface: A naturalist expands on the zebra, which returned in ancient times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' shuffles ON ZEBRA into BRONZEA; 'making come-back' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bronze Age is a prehistoric period when bronze tools were used.

clue.text: Energy required in open-and-shut case?

definitions.meaning: a fastener that opens and shuts a bag or case

explanation.definitionFit: Zip means energy; a zip fastener opens and shuts a case.

clue.text: Quiet chat with naval commander ignoring half the bursting shells

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
to rap is to chat

indicators.note: ignoring half drops the back half of the commander's name

parts.note: Nelson was Britain's famous naval commander

explanation.surface: A hushed talk with an admiral about shells exploding.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral Nelson is the naval commander; 'ignoring half' keeps the first half, NEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrapnel is fragments flung from exploding shells; the term once meant the shell itself.

clue.text: Promising in court to attend

parts.note: up means before the court, as in 'up before the magistrate'
to be at an event is to attend it

explanation.surface: Hopeful at a court appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' meaning on trial is British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means optimistic and positive, which is how promising news feels.
